SE(2)-equivariant models for robotic fault detection

Can geometric consistency under coordinate-frame transformations provide a lightweight and interpretable signal for online robotic fault monitoring?

SE(2) equivariance
Geometric machine learning
Anomaly detection
Robotic control
Locked validation · OOD testing
PyTorch · Python

Reproducibility archive ↗

Approach

We developed a lightweight neural controller and a detector combining equivariance residuals, kinematic deviations and command–observation mismatches. The detector was calibrated using healthy trajectories only.

Evaluation

The system was evaluated across eight simulated robotic fault types using locked validation, coordinate-frame and out-of-distribution stress tests, multi-seed regularisation ablations, fault-family controls and recovery-control ablations.

Finding

The detector achieved 0.8568 macro AUROC on the untouched locked q50 validation partition. Code, frozen protocols, checkpoints, raw outputs and figures are available in the reproducibility archive.

Limitations

The experiments are simulated and do not establish robustness on physical robots. Multi-seed uncertainty and non-significant effects are reported rather than folded into a stronger claim.
